findings: Full test_boundary.py text reading is now complete across Batches 76-78. This batch runs the complementary 25 offline instances; Batch 77 ran 17. Together 42 offline instances pass, with 13 live tests explicitly unexecuted.

Constructor/recording controls use injected complete transcripts. They verify argument guards, parse/error handling, declaration persistence and no model after abort, not correctness of the mocked mathematical output.

The full-loop field-relative emptiness test uses a synthetic BASE_EXTENSION edge whose endpoint models do not actually encode a field extension. It intentionally isolates the kernel transport cell; it is not evidence of concrete extension construction.

The positive UNIT_IDEAL_CERT base-change test declares a certificate kind without exhibiting a receipt. Its lack of hook findings tests transport classification, not earned leaf authority. The distinction matches the zero-path and explanation findings in Batches 51 and 67.

The offline right-inverse regression injects substitution strings and checks the verifier considers both compositions. Actual non-involution orientation, simultaneous substitution, nonreduced ideals and characteristic-sensitive live execution remain among excluded tests.

Live tests specify useful complementary controls: correct and incorrect unit certificates, characteristic-23 non-unit ideal, characteristic-two containment, mapped involution and translation orientation, and saturation/zero-ideal constructors. Earlier portable corpus controls cover selected mathematical questions but do not stand in for these unexecuted live paths.

The lazy availability probe is read as historical test harness code, not executed. It accepts either zero return code or a Singular banner and therefore is a reachability heuristic, not proof the specific mathematical backend operation works.
